text:
taylor: Heads-up — wearwave detector kicked for scratchpool eu-west2: forecast shows >75% of hot-stripes drifting toward threshold in the next 24h. could hit attach holds.

anita: Do we have a grafana link + what metric tripped? scrub backlog or raw SMART/wear counters?

ops-bot: ALERT: wearwave-analysis job=wearwave-2024-08-01 flagged pool= scratchpool-eu-west2, anomaly_score=0.84, affected_devices=3

bryan: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/scratch/wearwave?orgId=1&panelId=7 — shows wear_rate and spare_blocks climbing on 3 devices.

mike: For quick-check I ran: 
```
sum(rate(nvme_wear_bytes_total{pool="scratchpool-eu-west2"}[1h])) by (device)
```
Results: 3 devices ~9x baseline, others normal. Not just scrub backlog noise.

taylor: Ok. Impact: janitor might quarantine/readonly those devices and that will block GPU attach on nodes using them. We should avoid a fleet-wide attach pause if possible.

anita: Mitigation options:
 - throttle janitor concurrency for that pool
 - widen scrub window / reduce parallelism
 - temporarily prefer other regions for non-prod GPU jobs
 - proactively drain the 3 nodes if wear keeps climbing

bryan: Cost note: diverting ~200 non-prod GPUs to us-west1 for 24h == ~+12% estimated infra spend (egress + on-demand delta). Ticket and finance heads-up if we go that route.

sre-oncall: Immediate plan proposal: set janitor.concurrency=4 for scratchpool-eu-west2, reduce scrub parallelism, and add a 6h observation window. Open a replacement order for the flagged devices. If wear doesn't improve, do a canary swap off those nodes.

mike: Doing the config change now. Running:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/janitor JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=4 --record
```
Will also patch PoolConfig: `scrub.maxParallel=2` for scratchpool-eu-west2.

mike: Scheduler rule pushed to prefer us-west1 for job.priority<50 (non-prod). Deploy reference: https://git.internal/deploys/roll/7721

ops-bot: NOTE: rollout initiated — janitor concurrency env update (r234). 3 nodes acknowledged the change.

anita: Follow-ups: open INF ticket to replace the 3 flagged drives, tag nodes with `wear=high` and set eviction policy to `drain-after=12h` if wear rate still rising. Also add an alert to #costs for any regional diversion > 6h.

bryan: INF-4527 created, added cost estimate and assigned to hw-ops. Slack alert webhook added.

taylor: Good. If wear doesn't fall within 6h we start canary swap (move ~20 nodes out of rotation and replace). Keep this thread updated with wear_rate numbers. :thumbsup:

mike: Will post snapshots every hour. First snapshot uploaded to the ticket.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged and monitoring. I'll escalate to hw-ops if we see more devices cross the threshold.

taylor: thanks everyone. short-term tradeoff accepted (slightly higher cost) to avoid attach storm.
